sources.title: US service scope and used gear

layers.name: Core
layers.summary: Public statements prioritize useful gear, reduced unnecessary consumption and keeping products in use. This is a bounded observation, not proof of all organizational decisions.

layers.name: Skin
layers.summary: The historical advertisement and current service pages express reduction, repair and reuse in different contexts.

layers.name: Interconnections
layers.summary: The repair page publicly describes a relationship with iFixit for care and repair guides.

principles.name: Prioritize useful life — study inference
principles.definition: When gear remains useful or repairable, consider continued use before unnecessary replacement. A documented need and inability to restore useful performance can justify replacement.
principles.tradeoff: Accept fewer immediate replacement purchases when current gear can still meet the need.
principles.example: In the hypothetical exercise, consider repair for a fixable defect.
principles.counterexample: In the hypothetical exercise, encourage replacement of functional gear solely because a new season starts.

principles.name: Bound promises by their evidence — study rule
principles.definition: Do not turn a qualified public service or environmental statement into an unconditional promise.
principles.tradeoff: Accept a narrower message when support for a stronger promise is absent.
principles.example: Describe an available repair inquiry without promising a universal price or deadline.
principles.counterexample: Promise zero impact or guaranteed free repair within 48 hours based on a general service page.

checks.message: Study warning: an absolute environmental claim needs source review.
checks.suggestion: Remove the absolute claim or obtain evidence supporting its exact scope; do not invent a percentage.
